title: SecretRedaction
description: Normative shapes for agent/contracts/secret-redaction@1.0.0. Three documents live here and a document is exactly one of them: a redaction class declaration (what kind of material must not leave the wrapper in the clear, and how a value of that kind is recognised), a tool's optional secret-field declaration (which of a tool's argument and result fields carry which class), and the redacted reference that stands in a model request, a stored transcript, a ledger record and a replicated store where a secret value was. The class vocabulary is open - the product and a capability pack may declare a class - and the reference form is closed: a redacted reference carries the class and the field and nothing else (INV-AG-43). That closure is expressed here structurally rather than in prose: the reference object admits exactly three members, each constrained to a form no fragment of a value can be spelled in, and additionalProperties is false, so a hash, a truncation, a prefix, a length or a lookup key cannot be added to it without editing this file - which is a MAJOR revision of the contract. No measurement of redaction exists in this project: the coverage and false-positive behaviour of the recognition rules below is UNVERIFIED, and design.md R3 proposes spike SP-25 to measure it.

oneOf.title: RedactionClassDeclaration
oneOf.description: One named kind of material that must not leave the wrapper in the clear, declared by the product or contributed by a capability pack through its manifest's secretClasses member. A declaration is read at start (product) or at activation (pack); a declaration the boundary cannot compile is refused whole and the class does not exist, because a class that exists but cannot recognise anything is a class that reports protection it is not providing.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the secret-redaction contract this declaration is written against. A declaration written against a later version is refused whole rather than read around: reading around an unrecognised member of a class declaration means running with a recognition rule this build did not understand.

class.description: The class name, and the only thing about the class that a redacted reference carries. A class the product ships has a bare name; a class a capability pack contributes is prefixed with the pack identifier and a dot, which is what makes a collision between a pack's class and a shipped class impossible rather than merely detectable.

name.description: What the user sees where a redacted reference is displayed - in a ledger entry, a job detail, an approval request. Display text only; nothing reads it to decide anything.

origin.description: Where the declaration came from. A pack's classes are contributed when the pack activates and withdrawn when it deactivates, exactly as its tools, roles and skills are; an unactivated pack declares no class (INV-AG-45).

pack.description: The capability pack that contributed this class. Required when origin is 'pack', and must be the prefix segment of the class name.

description.description: Why this material must not be written down, in the words a reviewer of the class needs. Prose; carries no behaviour.

recognition.description: How a value of this class is recognised when no tool declared the field that carries it. This is the conservative default of D9: classification is declaration-first, and a field that was not declared but matches a rule here is redacted anyway, because an omission by a tool author must not become a disclosure. Coverage and false-positive rate are UNVERIFIED; proposed spike SP-25 measures both.

rules.description: The recognition rules, evaluated in the order given. An empty list is permitted and meaningful: the class is then declaration-only, redacted only where a tool named a field as carrying it, and the declaration says so in its description rather than implying a default it does not have.

rule.description: Stable identifier of this rule within its class, so a measurement or a false-positive report can name the rule that fired rather than the class.

appliesTo.description: What the pattern is tested against: the name of the field being projected, or the string value it holds. A field-name rule catches a well-named field whose tool forgot to declare it; a value rule catches material that arrived inside a payload under a name nobody could predict.

pattern.description: A regular expression. It is compiled when the declaration is read; a pattern that does not compile refuses the whole declaration (REDACTION_CLASS_INVALID), because a class whose rule silently never fires is worse than an absent class.

minLength.description: Optional lower bound on the length of a value a value-rule may classify, used to keep a broad pattern off short ordinary strings. It bounds nothing about the reference, which never carries a length.

description.description: What this rule is meant to catch and what it is known to over-catch. The honest place to record a suspected false positive before SP-25 measures one.

referenceForm.description: The only reference form there is. A class declaration names it rather than choosing it: the vocabulary of classes is open and the reference form is closed, so a new class cannot arrive carrying a new way of standing in for a value. A declaration naming anything else is refused.

oneOf.title: ToolSecretFieldDeclaration
oneOf.description: A tool's optional statement of which of its argument and result fields carry which redaction class. This is the value of the optional 'secrets' member that agent/contracts/tool-wrapping@0.2.0 adds to a tool registration, with the tool's name repeated so the document can be validated on its own. It is optional in the strict sense: no registration written against tool-wrapping@0.1.0 becomes invalid by its introduction, and a tool that declares nothing is still protected by the recognition rules of every declared class.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the secret-redaction contract this declaration is written against.

tool.description: The registered tool name this declaration belongs to - the same name the wrapping factory holds.

arguments.description: Argument fields that carry secret material. Declaring a field here does not change what the adapter receives: the adapter is given the unredacted arguments, and this declaration governs only the projection of what leaves the wrapper.

results.description: Result fields that carry secret material. A declaration here is an optimisation over the recognition rules, not a substitute for them: an undeclared result field matching a declared class's rule is redacted anyway.

oneOf.title: RedactedReference
oneOf.description: What stands in a model request, a stored transcript, a ledger record and a replicated store where a secret value was. It carries the class and the field and nothing else (INV-AG-43): it is not a key, not a hash of the value, not a truncation and not a length, because none of those is safe to replicate and replication is exactly what happens to it. Under principle VII replicated data is decryptable by the service by design, so the cheapest defence available is not writing the secret down. The closure is structural here: exactly three members, additionalProperties false, and both carried members constrained to forms in which no fragment of a value can be spelled - the class name is drawn from the declared vocabulary and the field path from the product's own traversal, never from the value and never from a platform's own key text.

redacted.description: The marker that makes a reference recognisable wherever it sits in an otherwise ordinary payload, so a reader can render it, an exporter can refuse it and the boundary can leave an already-projected value alone rather than projecting it twice (INV-AG-42: exactly once).

class.description: The class of material that was removed, naming a declared class. This is what makes the account of the step complete in everything except the secret itself, which is the recommended answer to Q-6 in the change's clarifications.md - owned by the ledger capability owner and not settled here.

field.description: Where in the projected document the value stood, as a traversal path. The record already says which side it belongs to - an intent record's parameters or a result record's response - so the side is not repeated here.

SchemaVersion.description: A three-part version of this contract.

ClassName.description: A declared class name: lower-case words joined by hyphens, optionally prefixed by a capability pack identifier and a dot. The shipped set is provider-credential, connector-authorisation-token, authorisation-code, refresh-token and personal-identifier. The pattern admits no character in which a token, a key or an identifier fragment could be smuggled into a replicated record.

FieldPath.description: A traversal path within the document being projected: dotted segments, with [] for every element of an array and [n] for one position. A segment of '*' stands for a key whose name this grammar cannot spell - a platform payload's own key text is untrusted content, and copying it into a reference would make the reference a second carrier of exactly what the boundary exists to stop. The grammar admits no quoting and no free text, so a path cannot be used to carry a value.

SecretField.description: One field of a tool's arguments or results, and the class of material it carries.

path.description: The field, as a traversal path within the arguments object or the result value. A path naming no member of the tool's declared parameter shape is refused at registration (SECRET_FIELD_PATH_UNKNOWN), where the tool's author sees it, rather than at the first call, where a user would.

class.description: A declared class. A path naming a class no declaration provides is refused at registration: a tool cannot invent a class, because the reference it would produce would name something no reader can explain.
